Custom packages are categorised three separate ways at once, plus a free-text field, and nothing in the
database says which one wins. Before they move to the new catalog schema that has to become one clean
tree. This workbook puts the systems side by side so people who know the business can decide.
THE THREE TABS — what each one actually is
TAB 1 · Collections            table: website_categories                    71 rows, 14 in use
A curated group with its own URL, which can hold packages AND supplements AND coach consultations
in the same group. The only place today where the product families already sit together.
IV Drip at Home · Lab Test at Home · Babysitting · Nursing Care · Supplements · Brands
Its category_type column says whether a row holds other groups (MULTI_GROUP, 42 rows) or holds
Read by: the supplement, coach-package and package-CMS repositories.
TAB 2 · Package categories     table: frontend_webpackagecategory           143 rows, 38 in use
Packages only, one level below a collection. This is the category a package is actually filed under
on the website, and it is reached from the package's CMS record — not from the package itself.
IV Therapy · Physiotherapy · DNA and Genetic Tests · Nurse Care · Functional Tests
Read by: CMSPackageRepository, i.e. the website listing and PDP.
TAB 3 · Order path             table: products_packages_products            116 rows, 48 in use
NOT customer-facing. This is the classification the cart, order and test-result code reads, and it is
never rendered as a menu — which is why it contains rows like 'Custom Order (Hidden Purpose)'.
It has the widest coverage of the three, but 52% of Active packages sit in just two inactive
Read by: CartServiceImpl, OrderUtils, TestResultServices — the money path.
Plus internal_category, a free-text field on both the package and the CMS row. Not a foreign key,
sparse, but where present often the cleanest signal of the three: DNA · Physio · IV · Babysitter.
NOT IN THIS WORKBOOK — the actual site menu
navigation_menus + navigation_menu_sub_categories drive the home page menu (HomePageController).
They have not been dumped. If 'sub-department' is meant to mirror what a customer sees in the menu,
that is the table to look at, and this workbook does not yet cover it.
SUB-DEPARTMENT AND CATEGORY ARE TWO DIFFERENT QUESTIONS — both are asked here
DEPARTMENT / SUB-DEPARTMENT     catalog_master.sub_department_id    EXACTLY ONE. Required.
What kind of thing this IS. Structural, permanent, country-agnostic, carries a stable machine code.
The schema calls it 'leaf classification; replaces item_type'. Two levels, via departments.parent_id:
TREATMENTS  →  IV Therapy · Physiotherapy         (to be defined)
HOMECARE    →  Babysitting · Elderly Care · Nursing Care
A package is filed against the SUB-department; the department follows from the tree, so you do not
have to keep them consistent by hand — the ► Department column is there to make the intended parent
ONE package = ONE sub-department. catalog_master.sub_department_id is a single column, so a package
cannot structurally belong to two. If something feels like it needs two — a home IV drip that is both
IV Therapy and Homecare — give it the single best structural home and express the second membership
as a CATEGORY instead. Flag it in Notes: if this happens a lot, the schema needs revisiting, and we
would much rather learn that from this sheet than after it ships.
CATEGORY         catalog_categories                    MANY per package. Optional.
Where it is BROWSABLE. Per country, per channel, freely re-arranged, many-to-many.
A package can sit in several; changing them is a merchandising decision, not a structural one.
Rule of thumb: if moving it would change what the product IS, it is a sub-department.
If it would only change where customers find it, it is a category.
On tabs 1-3 the ► Sub-department column asks: does this category correspond to a service line?
Most will be blank — 'Under 99 AED' is not a service line. On Package Reconciliation the
► Sub-department column is the per-package answer, and it is REQUIRED: every row in catalog_master
carries one, so a package with no answer cannot migrate.
Tabs 1 and 2 merge into ONE table in the new schema. `categories.is_category` is exactly MULTI_GROUP vs
PRODUCT — grouping node vs listing node — and category_relations gives the nesting. The ► Type column
on tab 1 is PRE-FILLED from category_type; please correct it rather than trusting it.
Amber ► columns are yours to fill. Everything else is exported data — please don't edit it, so the
sheet can be regenerated without losing your work.
Work tabs 1 → 2 → 3, not the package list. There are far fewer categories than packages, so a decision
per category settles most packages automatically. Use Package Reconciliation only for what is left over.
► Sub-department  does this category correspond to a service line? usually blank
► Action          keep it, merge it into another id, or drop it
► Type            grouping node (holds other categories) or listing node (holds packages)
► Parent          which category it sits under — the new schema allows more than one
► Show on app / ► Show on web    separate flags in the new schema, so app and web can differ
Package counts are split Active / Inactive, and the Usage column names the two cases that otherwise look
identical: 'empty' = nothing has ever pointed at it (safe to drop), 'dormant' = only inactive packages do
(look before dropping). 205 of the 330 category rows across the three tabs are empty.
Package Reconciliation lists Active AND Inactive packages — filter on Status.
THINGS TO KNOW BEFORE YOU START
· Two kinds of duplicate, needing different answers. 'Same name, other country' is a country pair —
'General Health' exists for UAE and KSA — and the new schema has one list with availability per
country, so those merge. The '⚠ Duplicate' column is the other kind: same name or slug within ONE
country. 'Physiotherapy at Home' is ids 3 and 13 on the same slug. One of those is junk, and seo_meta
has a UNIQUE constraint on (country, language, slug), so they cannot all migrate.
· Not every row is a category. Several are campaigns or partner buckets — 'Under 99 AED', 'Yellow Friday',
'Google Ads: Lab Test at Home', 'Mounjaro Cohort', 'Allianz Packages'. Mark those drop.
· 'Reachable on website' is derived from the website CMS record only. Whether the mobile app has its own
listing path has NOT been confirmed, so a package marked unreachable may still be live in the app.
Please flag any you know to be app-only.
